services.name: api-ingest
services.purpose: Receive external API requests and forward them to the message queue

services.name: message-queue
services.purpose: Buffer events between the API layer and worker services

services.name: worker-service
services.purpose: Consume messages from the queue, process them, and write results to the data warehouse

services.name: data-warehouse
services.purpose: Store processed data for analytics and reporting

dependencies.description: API layer publishes events to the message queue
Workers poll messages from the queue for processing
Workers write processed data into the warehouse

network.notes: All private services reside in private subnets of a VPC; API gateway is publicly accessible.

ambiguities.detail: The description did not specify a queue technology; SQS is the native AWS managed queue service.
ambiguities.assumption: Amazon SQS is used as the message queue.

ambiguities.detail: No runtime was mentioned; ECS Fargate provides a serverless container platform suitable for processing messages.
ambiguities.assumption: Workers run on Amazon ECS using Fargate launch type.

ambiguities.detail: The term "data warehouse" is ambiguous; Redshift is the primary AWS offering for columnar analytical storage.
ambiguities.assumption: Amazon Redshift is used as the data warehouse.

ambiguities.detail: The description only says "API ingest"; HTTPS through API Gateway is the typical secure entry point on AWS.
ambiguities.assumption: HTTPS via Amazon API Gateway is used for external access.

ambiguities.detail: Storing raw payloads is not described; S3 is the default object storage for such use cases.
ambiguities.assumption: Amazon S3 bucket stores raw incoming data before processing.

ambiguities.detail: No network layout was provided; this segmentation isolates internal components while exposing only the API.
ambiguities.assumption: All services run inside a single VPC with public subnet for API Gateway and private subnets for the queue, workers, and warehouse.
